generatingConcepts: Study historical change through the full UCR History sequence, source criticism and research, alongside archaeology, material and visual culture, media history, historiography and cultural memory. Ancient Greek, imperial, modern and Indigenous inquiries provide concrete historical cases, with digital data methods supporting source-based work.

Combine the full UCR History sequence with sustained study of political institutions, international order, law, rights and conflict. Historical source inquiry and contemporary institutional/legal analysis provide different methods for examining power and political change.

Combine the full UCR History sequence with economics, sociology, institutions and empirical methods to examine social change, inequality and political economy. Renaissance Mediterranean exchange adds a concrete early-modern cultural/economic connection; economic models complement rather than replace historical explanation.

candidates.label: Social and economic history, migration and inequality

selection.assessment: Closest material-cultural history, politics/conflict, then social/economic inquiry each pass independently at the limited first-two-year core scope. All retain substantive historical/source research and have different sustained adjacent curricula. Three is the maximum; no additional career- or example-generated slot.

strengthening: Added actual ancient Greek, Athenian citizenship, historical media-object and R spatial/text-data inquiry. Removed general literary/adaptation and school-rhetoric selections from the closest in favor of stronger historical objects/methods; third replaces organizational psychology/school rhetoric with historical Mediterranean exchange and digital data. No arbitrary distinctness repairs.
academicCoreTest: Six actual History courses sustain historical interpretation, primary-source research, historiographical critique and substantial inquiry; archaeology, visual/material history and media memory strengthen the closest rather than supply generic breadth. Political/legal and economic/social programs preserve that historical spine while genuinely changing explanatory priorities. Missing medieval/Dutch survey breadth and specialist textual/regional methods remain explicit. This supports a meaningful bachelor-level core response, not full disciplinary equivalence or hypothetical research filling final-year gaps.

adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Those final-year subjects, access conditions and culmination could materially change a full-degree comparison and are excluded. Known specialist gaps remain visible; no assumed project fills them.

adverseResolutions.resolution: Later required study emphasizes broad cultural, political, socioeconomic or digital historical inquiry and different research organization.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Do not import a guessed unit or credit. The three narrower core responses remain supported by current historical content and distinct taught methods; neither final-year equivalence nor a complete entrant pathway follows.
